name: When do kitchen cabinets need to be completely replaced instead of repaired?

mainEntity.name: When do kitchen cabinets need to be completely replaced instead of repaired?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabinets must be replaced if the core boxes suffer from water damage, mold growth, or sagging structural joints that cannot securely hold weight. You also need replacement when the current layout creates functional bottlenecks, such as a refrigerator blocking a doorway or inadequate counter workspace. Outdated modular cabinets often lack modern features like full-extension drawers, pull-out trash systems, or soft-close hardware. If the face frames are warped or the box materials are crumbling, cosmetic fixes will not last, making a complete tear-out and new installation the most durable investment.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace cabinets if boxes have water damage, structural sagging, failing frames, or if the layout no longer supports your kitchen workflow.
